tenses_found: past perfect (had said, had in the world was gone)
passive (was gone, was already done, was gotten ready)
relative clauses (who worked, that comes, who paid him)
subordinate clauses (because, so that, when, if)
participial clauses (stitching and rapping and tapping, dancing and skipping)
grammatical_complexity.notes: Past simple dominates, but past perfect, passive voice, relative clauses, and participial constructions appear as a noticeable minority. Subordinate clauses are frequent throughout. Roughly 20-25% of sentences contain level-3 structures.

cultural_reference_load.notes: Universal fairy tale setting. Christmas is known in LatAm. Elves are globally recognized folklore figures. No North American-specific customs or institutional references.

sentence_structure.notes: Mixed lengths with many compound-complex sentences joined by semicolons and conjunctions. Several sentences exceed 30 words. Subordinate clauses are frequent but not deeply nested. Average around 23 words when counting semicolon-separated units.

items.context: There was once a shoemaker, who worked very hard and was very honest
items.reason: Spanish 'once' means 'eleven.' A beginner could be confused reading 'There was eleven a shoemaker.' However, the fairy tale opening formula is widely recognized, and context makes the meaning recoverable. Mixed: the trap exists but context mitigates it.
